name: Annotations load from the best file present, and a damaged non-NPZ file stops the search
given: A 640x480 image cat.png, with auto-save at its default of True (config/settings.py:45). Four sidecar slots for it are empty on disk (no cat.npz, no cat_seg.txt, no cat_CM.npz, no cat.xml, no cat_createml.json) and two are filled: cat_coco.json, truncated mid-object so json.load cannot parse it, and cat.txt, a healthy YOLO Detection file holding exactly two lines, '0 0.5 0.5 0.2 0.1' and '1 0.25 0.75 0.1 0.2'.
when: The user selects cat.png in the file tree. ui/managers/file_navigation_manager.py:186 clears the in-memory segment list, then :203-206 calls FileManager.load_existing_mask(cat.png, image_size=(480, 640)) with the height/width taken from the already-loaded pixmap. The user then navigates to the next image in the folder.
then: load_existing_mask walks _LOAD_CHAIN in order (core/file_manager.py:128-136, loop at :173). Slot 1 '.npz' -> cat.npz does not exist, skipped at :175-176. Slot 2 '_seg.txt' -> does not exist, skipped. Slot 3 '_coco.json' -> cat_coco.json exists, so the chain commits to it. It is a non-NPZ format, but image_size was supplied by the caller, so the size-resolution block at :178-185 is skipped entirely. The dispatch at :194-195 calls load_coco_json (:602). json.load raises JSONDecodeError, which is caught by the loader's own 'except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError)' at :616, logged as 'Error loading COCO JSON from <path>: <e>' at :618, and the loader RETURNS NORMALLY at :619. Because no exception escapes the loader, the 'except Exception ... continue' handler at :202-204 never fires, and control reaches the unconditional 'return' at :205. The whole chain ends there. Result: segment_manager.segments == [] -- exactly 0 segments. cat.txt is never opened, so the two boxes it holds never reach memory: by the denormalization at :446-449 they would have been class_id 0 at (x1,y1,x2,y2) = (256, 216, 384, 264) and class_id 1 at (128, 312, 192, 408). Nothing is shown to the user: the caller's own try/except at file_navigation_manager.py:207-212 never fires either, because no exception was raised. Worse, the file tree still marks cat.png as annotated, because find_annotation_file (:139-151) walks the same chain but tests only os.path.exists and therefore returns cat_coco.json.
and: Navigating to the next image runs the auto-save BEFORE the switch, with no dirty check and no confirmation (file_navigation_manager.py:156-160; the multi-view path does the same at :270-274). save_single_view_output finds the segment list empty and takes the delete branch instead of the export branch: 'if not self.segment_manager.segments: self._delete_associated_files(...); return' (ui/managers/save_export_manager.py:106-109). _delete_associated_files (:523-529) calls delete_all_outputs (core/exporters/__init__.py:209-215), which iterates ALL SEVEN registered exporters -- not only the user's selected export formats -- and each exporter's delete_output os.removes its own output path if it exists, with no authorship, provenance or mtime check (e.g. core/exporters/yolo_detection.py:48-53). So both the truncated cat_coco.json AND the healthy, never-read cat.txt are permanently removed. The only feedback is a transient 'Deleted: cat_coco.json, cat.txt' notification (save_export_manager.py:536-538). There is no prompt and no undo.
parameters: Chain order, highest fidelity first, by filename suffix appended to os.path.splitext(image_path)[0]: '.npz' (NPZ mask tensor) > '_seg.txt' (YOLO Segmentation) > '_coco.json' (COCO JSON) > '_CM.npz' (NPZ Class Map) > '.xml' (Pascal VOC) > '_createml.json' (CreateML) > '.txt' (YOLO Detection). Defined at core/file_manager.py:128-136, mirroring LOAD_PRIORITY at core/exporters/__init__.py:73-81; a unit test keeps the two in sync (tests/unit/core/exporters/test_bbox_roundtrip.py:494-500). Selection predicate: the chain commits to the FIRST suffix whose file exists (os.path.exists, :175) and stops at the FIRST such loader that returns without raising (:205). Ranking is by format only -- never by file mtime, file size or content, so an older .npz outranks a newer .xml (test_bbox_roundtrip.py:484-492). image_size = (height, width) is required by every format except NPZ; if the caller omits it, it is resolved lazily the first time a non-NPZ slot is reached (:178-179) via _read_image_size (:207-222), which tries PyQt6 QImageReader (header-only) and falls back to a full cv2.imread(IMREAD_UNCHANGED) decode, returning None only if both fail; once resolved it is cached in the loop variable for the remaining iterations. Deletion side of the contract: delete_all_outputs covers all 7 registered formats (core/exporters/__init__.py:209-215); export_all never deletes (:189-197).
edgeCases: THE REAL FALL-THROUGH PREDICATE: the chain advances to the next format if and only if the loader RAISES out to :202-204. It is not 'non-NPZ stops the search' and not 'a failed parse stops the search' -- it is 'a loader that swallows its own error stops the search'. Five loaders swallow and stop: YOLO Seg catches (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) at :555-558; COCO catches (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) at :616-619; Pascal VOC catches (ET.ParseError, OSError) at :468-470; CreateML catches (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) at :505-507; YOLO Det catches (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) at :426-428 (moot for ordering -- it is last).

BOTH NPZ-FAMILY LOADERS FALL THROUGH ON STRUCTURAL CORRUPTION, not just '.npz'. _load_npz (:224-266) has no try/except at all. load_npz_class_map wraps np.load in a try that catches ONLY (OSError, ValueError) at :309. Verified empirically against the app's numpy 2.2.6: a 0-byte archive raises EOFError, random bytes raise pickle.UnpicklingError, a truncated zip raises zipfile.BadZipFile -- none of which is an OSError or a ValueError. So a damaged _CM.npz propagates to :202 and the chain CONTINUES to .xml.

A _CM.npz stops the chain only on CONTENT failures: a missing 'class_map' key (:298-300) or a class_map whose shape[:2] differs from image_size (:313-318). Both log an error and return normally, so the chain halts with 0 segments.

ZERO SEGMENTS WITHOUT ANY ERROR also stops the chain (the same :205 return): a .npz that opens cleanly but has neither a 'mask' nor a 'masks' key returns at :241-242; a .npz whose mask channels are all empty appends nothing (:255-257); a CreateML file whose top level is not a list, is empty, or whose first element is not a dict returns silently at :509-510; a COCO file whose root is not an object logs and returns at :621-623; a file whose every record is rejected by its own per-line filter loads nothing.

Per-line filters: YOLO Detection accepts a line only if it splits into exactly 5 tokens (:433-434) whose last 4 parse as floats (:439-440). YOLO Segmentation accepts a line only if it has at least 7 tokens AND an odd token count (:564-565), all coordinates parse as floats (:569-570), and it yields at least 3 points (:573-574). Rejected lines are skipped silently, not raised.

IMAGE SIZE FAILURE ABORTS THE WHOLE CHAIN, not just one format. When a non-NPZ slot is reached with image_size still None and _read_image_size returns None (both QImageReader and cv2.imread failed), :180-185 logs 'Cannot load {fmt} annotations: image size unavailable for {path}' and RETURNS -- no later format is attempted. Reachable from the callers that pass no size: ui/main_window.py:3619 (sequence frame) and :4864 (multi-view -> single-view restore), and from :6112-6114 which may pass None. Fixed for the common paths in release 2.0.8 (CHANGELOG.md:12) by adding the header read; the abort branch remains.

PARTIAL STATE IS NEVER ROLLED BACK. :202-204 logs and continues without undoing anything the failed loader already did, and SegmentManager.add_segment appends without merging (core/segment_manager.py:28-56), so the next format's segments land on top and duplicate. Concrete trigger: Python's json.load accepts a bare Infinity literal, and the COCO loader's int(round(v)) then raises OverflowError at :659 (polygon branch) or :687 (bbox branch), which the 'except (TypeError, ValueError)' clauses at :662 and :690 do NOT catch -- while a NaN raises ValueError and IS caught, merely skipping that record. So a COCO file with an Infinity coordinate can register its category aliases (:626-637) and add several segments (:672-680), then raise, and the chain continues and appends Pascal VOC or YOLO Det segments on top of them. _load_npz has the same shape: it calls _restore_aliases at :232 before reading any mask data, so a NPZ that raises during the mask read still leaves its class aliases behind.
DISCOVERY IS BY SUFFIX ONLY, with no content sniffing and no ownership check, so any same-named file is parsed as that format -- a hand-written notes file cat.txt is fed to the YOLO Detection loader.

BASE-NAME COLLISIONS ACROSS IMAGES, with a worked consequence: for image foo_CM.png the base is 'foo_CM', so its '.npz' slot resolves to foo_CM.npz, which is foo.png's class map. That file opens cleanly but has no 'mask'/'masks' key, so _load_npz returns at :241-242 with 0 segments and the chain stops -- and the following auto-save then deletes foo.png's class map. foo_seg.png does the same to foo.png's foo_seg.txt (its 5-token detection lines are rejected at :564). foo.png and foo.jpg share every sidecar outright.

STALE HIGHER-PRIORITY FILES WIN. Switching the export format from NPZ to Pascal VOC leaves the old .npz in place -- export_all never deletes (core/exporters/__init__.py:189-197) -- and the chain still reads the stale .npz instead of the newer .xml. On save, the loaded content is written back over the selected formats, so browsing past an image can downgrade masks to boxes.

find_annotation_file (:139-151) checks existence only, so its answer and the chain's result can disagree: with a corrupt cat.npz plus a valid cat.txt, it reports cat.npz while cat.txt is what actually loads; with a truncated cat_coco.json it reports the image as annotated after 0 segments loaded. That answer drives which frames sequence propagation skips as already labelled (ui/main_window.py:4218-4227) and which count as reference frames (:3966), so a damaged sidecar can shield an image from propagation while contributing nothing.

TEST COVERAGE TODAY pins only the NPZ leg: test_bbox_roundtrip.py:741-747 (a corrupt .npz does not raise) and :749-756 (a corrupt .npz falls through to a valid .txt). None of the other six loaders has a fall-through or stop-the-chain test, which is why the swallow-and-stop behavior drifted away from the documented intent unnoticed.

SECURITY NOTE, adjacent but load-bearing for the rewrite: both NPZ loaders call np.load(..., allow_pickle=True) (:231 and :297), so a crafted .npz or _CM.npz sitting next to an image executes arbitrary code on open. The TypeScript rewrite must not reproduce a deserializer with that property.
answer: ANSWER TO THE OPEN QUESTION -- split the legacy behavior in two. THE CONTRACT the rewrite must reproduce exactly is the priority order and the first-existing-file selection: .npz > _seg.txt > _coco.json > _CM.npz > .xml > _createml.json > .txt (core/file_manager.py:128-136, mirroring core/exporters/__init__.py:73-81), chosen by format rank alone and never by mtime or content (test_bbox_roundtrip.py:484-492), because the loaded content is written straight back on the next auto-save and a reordered chain would silently rewrite pixel masks as rectangles. THE DEFECT the rewrite must NOT reproduce is everything downstream of a failed read: five of the seven loaders swallow their own read/parse error and return normally (:555-558, :616-619, :468-470, :505-507, :426-428), so no exception reaches the handler at :202-204 and the unconditional return at :205 ends the chain with 0 segments and a healthy lower-priority file unread; the empty segment list is then indistinguishable from an unannotated image, and the auto-save that runs on the next navigation (config/settings.py:45, file_navigation_manager.py:156-160) routes it to the delete branch (save_export_manager.py:106-109) and erases all seven sidecars including the one that was never read (exporters/__init__.py:209-215, yolo_detection.py:48-53). That this is a defect and not policy is settled in the repo itself: the docstring at core/file_manager.py:160-163, CHANGELOG.md:24 and src/lazylabel/ARCHITECTURE.md:204-207 all promise the chain moves past a damaged file, ARCHITECTURE.md:193 asserts delete_all_outputs runs only when the user cleared the annotations (nothing enforces that), and CHANGELOG.md:12 records release 2.0.8 fixing the OTHER cause of this identical data-loss sequence (the missing-image_size early return) while leaving the swallow-and-stop cause in place. Per the approved decisions, the rewrite must (a) continue the chain past any failed load, (b) surface the failure as a distinct 'load failed' state that is never equal to 'no annotations', and (c) delete annotation files only on an explicit user action -- never as an inferred consequence of an empty in-memory list. WHAT THE CARD GOT WRONG: (1) its title, plainEnglish and the edge case 'Only a corrupt .npz (np.load raises) falls through to the next format' are over-broad -- load_npz_class_map catches only (OSError, ValueError) at core/file_manager.py:309, and I verified against the app's numpy 2.2.6 that a 0-byte, garbage or truncated _CM.npz raises EOFError, pickle.UnpicklingError or zipfile.BadZipFile respectively, none of which is caught, so a structurally damaged _CM.npz ALSO falls through; the correct predicate is 'the loader raises', and only its content failures (missing class_map at :298-300, shape mismatch at :313-318) stop the chain; (2) it framed the winner as 'the first format present' when the code's winner is the first existing file whose loader returns without raising (:173-176 commits, :202-204 continues, :205 stops); (3) it omitted the stop-with-zero-and-no-error cases -- a .npz with no mask key (:241-242), a non-list CreateML root (:509-510), a non-object COCO root (:621-623); (4) it carried three near-duplicate image-size edge cases and described the size read as 'header-only', when _read_image_size (:207-222) tries QImageReader header-only and then falls back to a full cv2.imread decode, is resolved lazily on the first non-NPZ hit and cached for the rest of the loop, and aborts the entire chain rather than skipping one format (:180-185); (5) its 'and' field was null, leaving the destructive tail uncited; (6) its partial-state edge case named no trigger -- the real one is an Infinity coordinate in COCO raising OverflowError at :659/:687, uncaught by the (TypeError, ValueError) clauses at :662/:690 (a NaN raises ValueError and IS caught, merely skipping that record). WHAT AN IMPLEMENTER MUST WATCH FOR: model the loader outcome as a three-way result -- LOADED(n segments) / EMPTY(file parsed, genuinely no objects) / FAILED(unreadable) -- because the legacy code collapses FAILED into EMPTY and that collapse is the whole bug; keep existence-check and load-result as separate answers, since find_annotation_file (:139-151) tests only os.path.exists and its verdict drives sequence propagation (ui/main_window.py:3966, :4218-4227); make the seven suffixes a single table shared by loader, writer and deleter so the order cannot drift (the legacy sync is guaranteed only by test_bbox_roundtrip.py:494-500); do not carry over allow_pickle-style deserialization (:231, :297); and treat the base-name suffix collisions (foo_CM.png, foo_seg.png, foo.png vs foo.jpg) as a real hazard, since they produce a zero-segment load on one image that deletes another image's sidecar.
corrections: Narrowed the rule's central claim: replaced 'a damaged non-NPZ file stops the search' with 'the chain continues only when a loader raises' -- a structurally corrupt _CM.npz also falls through (file_manager.py:309 catches only (OSError, ValueError); numpy 2.2.6 raises EOFError / pickle.UnpicklingError / zipfile.BadZipFile, verified empirically).

Replaced the edge case 'Only a corrupt .npz (np.load raises) falls through to the next format' with the two-loader version, and listed the five loaders that genuinely swallow-and-stop with their exact catch tuples and line numbers.

Restated the selection predicate as 'the first existing file whose loader returns without raising' (:173-176 / :202-204 / :205), replacing both 'the first format present' and any 'first that loads something' reading.

Added the stop-with-zero-segments-and-no-error cases the card omitted: .npz with no mask/masks key (:241-242), all-empty mask channels, CreateML non-list root (:509-510), COCO non-object root (:621-623).

Merged the card's three duplicate image-size edge cases into one and corrected the mechanics: QImageReader header read with a full cv2.imread fallback (:207-222), resolved lazily on the first non-NPZ hit and cached for the rest of the loop (:178-179), and aborting the WHOLE chain rather than one format (:180-185); named the callers that reach it (main_window.py:3619, :4864, :6112-6114).

Filled the previously null 'and' field with the fully cited destructive tail: settings.py:45 -> file_navigation_manager.py:156-160 -> save_export_manager.py:106-109 -> :523-529 -> exporters/__init__.py:209-215 -> yolo_detection.py:48-53, plus the 'Deleted:' toast at :536-538.

Made the 'then' a complete worked trace with real numbers, including the two boxes cat.txt would have produced -- class 0 at (256, 216, 384, 264) and class 1 at (128, 312, 192, 408) at 640x480, per the denormalization at :446-449.

Named the concrete trigger for the mixed-state edge case: a COCO Infinity coordinate raising OverflowError at :659/:687, uncaught by the (TypeError, ValueError) handlers at :662/:690, versus NaN which raises ValueError and is caught; added _restore_aliases at :232 as the NPZ equivalent.

Added the find_annotation_file aggravator (:139-151): existence-only, so it disagrees with the chain's actual result and still marks a zero-segment image as annotated, driving propagation skips at main_window.py:3966 / :4218-4227.

Gave the base-name-collision edge case a worked consequence (foo_CM.png loads foo.png's class map, gets 0 segments, then auto-save deletes foo.png's class map) instead of stating the collision abstractly.

Corrected the provenance in the defect claim: CHANGELOG.md:12 (2.0.8) fixed the missing-image_size cause of this same data-loss sequence but not the swallow-and-stop cause; CHANGELOG.md:24, ARCHITECTURE.md:204-207 and the docstring at file_manager.py:160-163 all state the fall-through intent, and ARCHITECTURE.md:193 asserts a user-cleared precondition for delete_all_outputs that nothing enforces.
Added the test-coverage edge case: only the NPZ leg is pinned (test_bbox_roundtrip.py:741-756); the LOAD_PRIORITY/_LOAD_CHAIN sync rests on test_bbox_roundtrip.py:494-500.
Added a security note on np.load(allow_pickle=True) at :231 and :297 so the rewrite does not reproduce a code-executing deserializer.
Answered the open question explicitly: the priority order is the contract to reproduce; the silent empty load and the delete-on-empty that follows are the defect to fix.
unresolved: Three product decisions remain. (1) Sidecar namespacing: legacy discovery is pure suffix matching on the image base name, so foo.png, foo.jpg, foo_seg.png and foo_CM.png share or steal each other's sidecars. Fixing this changes which file an existing dataset loads, so it cannot be decided from the code alone. (2) How a failed load must be surfaced -- a blocking modal, a persistent per-image banner, or a badge in the file tree -- given the approved rule that it must never present as 'no annotations'; the legacy path shows nothing at all. (3) When the chain continues past a loader that already added some segments, whether the rewrite should discard that partial result (clean per-format transaction) or keep and merge it as the legacy does; the legacy behavior produces duplicates and is almost certainly unintended, but choosing discard changes observable output for COCO files with Infinity coordinates.
